content:
Alex: Heads up — production alert from NovaDocs. Customer reporting spike in 5xx and p95 timeouts for hosted inference since ~09:20 UTC. Several 504 gateway timeouts.
Priya: Got it. Any request ids or sample timestamps?
Alex: Sent request ids in the ticket: rq_92a1f, rq_92a2b, rq_92a7c. Their SLA says worst-case p95 ~3s but they're seeing 8–12s followed by 504. Logs show repeated \"enqueue timeout\" messages.
Jamal: I pulled runtime metrics for their tenant. Queue depth is spiking above the configured soft limit, continuous-batcher backlog grows, dequeue throughput drops. KV cache misses spike right before the tail timeouts.
Priya: Can you paste the critical logs? Need to know whether it's batching backlog or an auth/billing throttle.
Jamal: Paste below (redacted):
```
[09:18:42] tenant=novadocs enqueue_latency_ms=1200 queue_depth=128 kvcache_miss=0.87 batch_size=1
[09:18:43] tenant=novadocs dequeue_error=timeout handler=batcher reason="no-available-worker"
[09:19:05] tenant=novadocs enqueue_latency_ms=2560 queue_depth=312 kvcache_miss=0.91 batch_size=1
[09:19:05] gateway 504 request_id=rq_92a1f route=/v1/generate
[09:19:07] auth service: token-lookup=ok billing-check=ok
[09:19:10] batcher-stats: active_workers=0 pending_batches=45
```
Priya: Interesting — auth/billing checks are OK per log, so likely resource exhaustion. infra-bot, any infra alerts correlated?
infra-bot: [ALERT] hostpool-us-east-3 GPU utilization 98% (09:16–09:22), batcher service restarted automatically at 09:20:33 due to OOM.
Alex: Customer says it started after a traffic spike from a 3rd-party integration. They didn't change model or prompt.
Jamal: Repro steps for support to capture: 1) capture `X-Request-Id` header for any failing call; 2) set `X-Debug-Trace: true` and include raw latency breakdown; 3) curl the /_internal/queue-metrics endpoint with tenant header to capture live queue_depth/kvcache rate. Example: `curl -H "X-Tenant: novadocs" https://infra.internal/_internal/queue-metrics`
Priya: For mitigations — short-term: route that tenant to a lower-qps dedicated pool (if available) or enable our fallback model variant to reduce GPU memory pressure. Also temporarily raise the soft queue_depth threshold for hosted gateway for that tenant.
Lena: I'll coordinate customer comms. We should offer 24h credits for the impacted window and explain mitigation steps. Keep it factual.
Jamal: Quick fix I pushed: increased per-tenant queue soft limit from 200 -> 400 and enabled a 2-minute auto-fallback to smaller model for tenants crossing 90% GPU util. Monitoring in place.
Alex: Confirmed with NovaDocs — errors dropped after ~09:28 and p95 back to normal, but they still saw intermittent 504s until 09:30.
Priya: Postmortem checklist: 1) root cause: continuous-batcher backlog + high kvcache miss during microburst. 2) action items: add spike protection on ingress (token-bucket smoothing), pre-warm KV cache on tenant warmups, add alert for batcher worker restarts. 3) check autoscaler configs for hostpool-us-east-3.
Lena: Assigning followups: @Jamal to run kvcache warmup plan, @Priya to update runbook, @Alex to finalize customer note.
Alex: Noted. I'll follow up in support ticket with timeline and credits. :+1:
Jamal: I'll open an infra PR to adjust the autoscaler thresholds and add a small internal test harness to replay microbursts.
Priya: Leaving this thread open until the PRs are merged and we verify no regression in the next 24h.
